chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Sin'an, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: When a believer dies and forty believing men stand over his corpse and they say, 'O God! We know nothing but good things about him and You know him better than we do,' the Blessed the Sublime God will say, 'I accepted your testimony regarding him and forgive him regarding whatever I know, but you do not know about him.'
ai.seo_question: How does the testimony of forty believers affect the forgiveness of a deceased person in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to emphasize the power of communal testimony (shahadat al--thalatha) in interceding for the deceased, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the social dimension of faith and collective merit. The divine response, 'I have accepted your testimony,' underscores the concept of divine grace extending beyond individual accountability to include the validation of the community's perception of the believer's piety. This mechanism illustrates how human witness, when sincere, becomes a conduit for Allah's mercy, forgiving sins that even the witnesses were unaware of.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-4 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Miskan thatAba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

What would happen when a believer dies and forty believing men stand over his corpse and they say, ‘O God! We know nothing but good things bout him and You know him better than we do’ is that the Blessed the Sublime God will say, ‘I accepted your testimony regarding him and forgive him regarding whatever I know, but you do not know about him.’”
